name: Opportunity Rover
goal: Search for geological evidence of ancient liquid water and assess past Martian habitability.
story: Landed on Mars in 2004 for a planned 90-day mission, Opportunity explored the Red Planet for over 15 years, traveling 28 miles. It discovered hematite blueberries and gypsum veins—conclusive proof that liquid water once flowed across Mars surface. A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 cut off its solar power, leaving the silent geologist on Meridiani Planum.

evidence.text: Opportunity discovered hematite blueberries and gypsum veins, proving liquid water was long-standing on ancient Mars.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Meridiani Planum once featured a mild, wet surface environment suitable for potential ancient microbial life.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: Whether any ancient Martian watery environment actually harbored microscopic life or preserved organic biosignatures.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Accrued 45.16 km (28.06 miles) of driving, setting the off-Earth distance record that held until 2026. Proved long-standing liquid water existed on Mars.

openQuestion.prompt: Opportunity proved Mars once had liquid water. What should a future rover search for next?
choices: Preserved organic biosignatures of ancient microbial life
How the Martian atmosphere and surface water disappeared over time
Geological rock layers in an unexplored crater basin

sources.title: NASA's Opportunity Rover Mission on Mars Comes to End

name: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)
goal: Provide mobility for Apollo astronauts on the lunar surface to extend exploration range and sample collection.
story: Deployed during Apollo 15, 16, and 17, the Moon Buggy allowed astronauts to travel tens of kilometers across craters and highlands. Traversing 36 km total, Apollo 17 set the lunar speed record of 11.2 mph. The three rovers remain parked on the Moon as historic monuments to human exploration.

evidence.text: Apollo LRVs extended astronaut exploration range up to 7.6 km from the Lunar Module, enabling collection of key highland rock samples.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Mobility across varied lunar terrain significantly increased scientific yield compared to foot-only lunar traverses.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: How decades of extreme lunar temperature swings, solar radiation, and micrometeorite impacts affected the rover structural alloys.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Demonstrated successful off-Earth manned mobility, logging 90.5 km total across three Apollo missions.

openQuestion.prompt: The LRVs sit silently on the Moon. What key lesson should future lunar rovers take from their design?
choices: Dust-resistant mesh wheel designs for fine lunar regolith
High-efficiency solar and thermal battery management
Autonomous navigation for tele-operated surface scouting

name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
goal: Demonstrate powered, controlled flight in the extremely thin Martian atmosphere.
payload: Solar Array and Lithium-Ion Battery Pack
story: Arriving on Mars in 2021, Ingenuity achieved the first powered flight on another world—a historic Wright Brothers moment. Designed for a 30-day demo of just 5 flights, it completed 72 flights over 3 years, serving as an aerial scout for Perseverance before rotor blade damage ended flight operations in January 2024.

evidence.text: Completed 72 successful powered flights covering 17.0 km at altitudes up to 24 meters in Mars thin atmosphere.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Aerial scouting accelerates rover surface science by identifying safe driving pathways and high-priority geological targets.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: How multi-rotor aerial vehicles will navigate intense Martian dust storms and carry heavy scientific instrument payloads.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Proved powered aerodynamic flight is possible on Mars, establishing a new dimension of aerial planetary exploration.

openQuestion.prompt: Ingenuity proved aerial exploration works on Mars. What capability should next-generation Mars helicopters possess?
choices: Mapping subsurface water ice deposits from low flight altitudes
Transporting geological rock samples across steep crater walls
Scouting unmapped Martian lava tubes and subsurface caves
